records.description: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center says on 8 October 2026 that El Niño continues to strengthen, with eastern equatorial Pacific sea surface temperatures more than 4.0C above average in places. records.title: IATTC shortens eastern Pacific tuna purse seine closure to 64 days but leaves FAD reforms unfinished
records.description: At its 103rd meeting in September 2025 the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission reduced the purse seine closure by eight days to 64 days for one year, citing healthy bigeye, yellowfin and skipjack stocks, and expanded the requirement to keep satellite FAD buoys transmitting south of 10 degrees S and west of 100 degrees W. The ISSF notes that broader FAD reforms such as a register were not addressed; the IATTC page for 2026 lists 64-day closures and 10 to 22 extra days for vessels above the 1,200 t bigeye limit. At its September 2026 meeting in Lisbon the IATTC reached no consensus on new tropical tuna measures, so the 2025 measure stays in force; NOAA Fisheries says the United States opposed proposed increases in purse seine capacity, members rolled over the "fins naturally attached" shark measure and adopted the Commission's first management procedure, for Pacific bluefin tuna.

records.title: Tulane-led study says relative sea-level rise in coastal Louisiana may be three times the global average
records.description: A Nature Sustainability study led by Tulane geologist Torbjorn Tornqvist, reported on 5 May 2026, says sea-level rise in coastal Louisiana may be about three times the global average because the land is subsiding. It finds that nearly all of Louisiana's coastal zone has lost residents since 2000, especially after major hurricanes, and urges planning now for relocation. The Gulf is expected to reach an ancient shoreline about 30 miles north of New Orleans, with no timeline given. The state's Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority chairman disputed the study on 27 May 2026.
